title: tried 5 locations, different scents to try to eliminate, all failed.
text:
tried 5 locations, different scents to try to eliminate, all failed.. EDIT: I am keeping my testing time going in the closed room with off smell (trial #5 as listed below). I think I have noticed a reduced odor in that room after 2.5 days running this 24/7. I will now unplug it and see if the odor returns. THEN I will once again come back to this review and make changes to rating (or keep same). I kept rest of review the exact same.
-------------------------------------------
Yes.. no.. maybe? (ultimately no).
Here are all my thoughts and observations, followed by my experience:

--It has a rotatable plug!! So if you go to plug it in and the prongs seem backward.. just turn it until it is the way you want it. Also allows you to plug it into a side ways receptacle and still be able to keep the unit upright. It can be a a little top heavy if your outlet isn't tight. Some outlets this feels firmly plugged in, and one of my other outlets is seems to back away from the wall a little. However, it still turns on and stays on.

--As expected from a UV-C bulb, it has a blue light emitting bulb. Don't stare at it. The bulb isn't exposed, but the light is still visible.

--Makes some noise when it is turned on. It isn't too loud (soft fan white noise), but it might be too loud for some depending where you put it.

--You will need to replace the bulb. Says it has MAX 5000 hours of life, so AT LEAST once per year. You know it is in need of replacement if the light is getting more dim, or better yet you can just make a plan to change it out every 6-8 months. No mention of where/how to buy replacements, though.

--Air is pulled into the closed system and it is with exposure to the light that the germs are annihilated. This does not sanitize/disinfect surfaces. It is strictly air borne. No filter as this type of purification doesn't require it. Depending on your needs, from what I have read using something like this along with a filter (hepa or electrostatic) type air purifier may make for best combo.

--The instructions say that, "it needs about 2 hours in 10 square meters of room" to start to gain benefit of disinfection. Small room, small space for best results (ie; 10'x10' room or less).

--From what I can surmise, this is for killing "airborne germs and odors".. so not for germs and such that have settled onto/into surfaces. It pulls air into through the cover, and from there the air and whatever is in it is exposed to the UV light HENCE why it will work best in smaller spaces. I do not know how much air it is able to pull through, or how far reaching it is. But closed, small rooms are likely to gain greatest and quickest benefit.

--Uses a UV-C bulb. "UV-C carries the most energy capable of destroying the bonds that hold together the DNA and RNA of viruses and bacteria, stopping them from working. The same sanitizing energy can also damage eyes and skin, and cause cancer". Do not stare at the bulb! Fortunately this bulb is covered and there is just a ring of light that can be detected. Even so, be mindful of not gazing at it.

--Ozone? UV illuminant: 253nm UV-C bulb ...at wavelengths shorter than 250 nanometres, they produce ozone, which is emitted out into the environment. So this just exceeds the threshold. Seems this is accurate in their saying that it does not emit ozone. Phew!

--VOCS? Information in packet alludes to it by stating, "If present in the environment, it will help eliminate formaldehyde" (which is an example of a VOC) So it may help in reducing off gassing from new products, or really old products, etc

--While a UV filter will not remove particulate matter, it can eliminate germs, bacteria, and viruses. As microorganisms in the air pass through the filter, UV rays will kill them. This ensures that common allergens and health-risks are eliminated in your home.

My experience?
Eh. No.

I have tried it in various areas: Trials 1-4 have too many variables to be able to determine if it is specifically this working. When it occurred to me to try option #5, I knew I had a winner, since it was one area that isn't getting air flow and it always has an off aroma, and I would be able to tell in short order if this is working or not. There would be nothing else to impact the way the room smelled. I would either smell the room or I wouldn't. So this is what /where I tried:

1. In our fully carpeted small bedroom where we sleep with our two big labs. (my large air purifier w/filter works, not sure about this. had it going for 6 hours prior to bed. No change. Unplugged it for sleep as the blue light illuminated the wall)

2. In a small room that has a couple of litter boxes set up. (Really couldn't tell)

3. In a small bathroom where we keep the door shut. It tends to have a weird smell in there despite being "clean". But it is still a lot of going in and out, and there is fluctuation of sense of weird smell. (can't tell for sure, but may consider this room for potential germ killing aspect anyway and use it for next 6-8 months)

4.. In a small area, near a litter box. The box is situated at the base of a set of stairs. While it is an open area, the air flow is stagnant. Curiously, shortly after plugging this in, I found the area to smell worse. I partly wonder if it was still early on and was actually pulling the odors out (therefor making it smell stronger?). I didn't see any fresh deposits made to the box. I didn't give it enough time to determine if it dissipates. I plugged my other definitely effective mini air purifier back in (non UV-C) and the air smelled cleaned up shortly after.
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B087JHKTRP/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_dp

5. Final test location: In a small 10'x10' guest room where the door is always shut, and rarely opened. The room has an odd odor. Our house is old and really nothing has been updated since maybe the 70s, at least 30 years before my husband bought it right out of college, and we haven't done anything to it. I imagine there is off gassing from old wallpaper, carpet, furniture, etc. It isn't musty, it is just.. odd. Was really hoping to smell a change. I checked in at 2 hours (still smells) and again 4 hours later (still smells, no change - at all). At the time I am writing this, I still have it plugged in in that room. If I notice any spectacular change I will come back to edit.

So, not a product for me. The only other spot I could consider trying is in the kitchen area (maybe food smells?) IF I can find a spot to plug it in. Options are limited, so I likely won't make a spot for it. It is big and depending on your receptacle, it may take up two outlets.

There just isn't enough information about the product or the company to make me feel secure in this being an effective item. If I could have at least smelled the difference, then I would feel better. I see that there are a couple of other "companies" selling exact same model, which really isn't doing anything to increase my trust. However, if I experience anything different I will be back to update. Mixed reviews here, so maybe I missing something in my trials?
